warnings: Scanned page image is authoritative; no selectable text layer.

candidates.name: Reaction stoichiometry
candidates.definition: Using mole ratios from a balanced equation to relate amounts of reactants and products by mass, moles, solution volume or gas volume.
candidates.include: Tag when an amount of one substance must be calculated from another through a balanced equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the stoichiometry is part of a titration (tag titration-analysis) or electrolysis (tag electrolysis-faraday) unless it is a separate requested calculation.

candidates.name: Dipole-dipole attractions
candidates.definition: Attractions between the permanent dipoles of polar molecules.
candidates.include: Tag when dipole-dipole forces must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hydrogen bonding cases unless the comparison involves dipole-dipole forces specifically.

candidates.name: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
candidates.definition: Using the relative strength of intermolecular forces to explain or rank boiling point, melting point, vapor pressure, viscosity, surface tension or enthalpy of vaporization, and distinguishing intermolecular from intramolecular forces.
candidates.include: Tag when a physical property must be compared or explained in terms of intermolecular attractions; pair with the specific force concept(s) that decide the comparison.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag chemical reactivity or bond-breaking explanations; boiling does not break covalent bonds.

candidates.name: Hydrogen bonding
candidates.definition: The strong dipole attraction between an H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F atom.
candidates.include: Tag when hydrogen bonding must be identified, drawn, or used to explain a property, including identifying donors and acceptors.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag molecules that contain H and O but no H bonded to N, O or F (a common error).

candidates.name: London dispersion forces
candidates.definition: Attractions arising from temporary dipoles, whose strength increases with the number of electrons (polarizability) and with contact surface area.
candidates.include: Tag when dispersion forces must be identified or compared, especially using polarizability or molecular shape.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag merely because dispersion forces exist in every substance; tag only when they matter to the answer.

candidates.name: Reaction mechanisms and intermediates
candidates.definition: Combining elementary steps into an overall equation, and identifying intermediates (formed then consumed) and catalysts (consumed then regenerated).
candidates.include: Tag when a mechanism's steps must be added or intermediates and catalysts identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag rate-law derivation from the mechanism (tag mechanism-rate-law) unless steps are also combined.

candidates.name: Catalysis
candidates.definition: How catalysts increase rate by providing an alternative mechanism with lower activation energy while being regenerated and leaving ΔH and K unchanged.
candidates.include: Tag when a catalyst's effect on mechanism, energy profile, rate, ΔH or equilibrium must be identified or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag intermediates questions without a catalyst.

candidates.name: Limiting reactant and yield
candidates.definition: Identifying the limiting reactant, calculating theoretical yield and excess reactant remaining, and calculating percent yield.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must decide which reactant limits the reaction, or compute theoretical, actual or percent yield.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag single-reactant stoichiometry with an obvious excess stated.

candidates.name: Mechanisms and rate laws
candidates.definition: Deriving the rate law predicted by a mechanism from its slow step, including fast pre-equilibrium steps that eliminate intermediates, and testing mechanisms against experimental rate laws.
candidates.include: Tag when a rate law must be derived from a mechanism, or a mechanism judged consistent with an observed rate law.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag experimental order determination with no mechanism.

candidates.name: Titration stoichiometry
candidates.definition: Using the volume of a standard solution needed to reach the equivalence point, together with the balanced equation, to find an unknown amount or concentration; includes equivalence point versus endpoint and buret reading.
candidates.include: Tag when titration data must be used to find an unknown quantity, or titration procedure and terminology are assessed.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag pH-curve shape questions (tag titration-curves) unless the equivalence volume is used for a calculation.

candidates.name: Acid-base titration curves
candidates.definition: Interpreting pH titration curves: equivalence-point pH, half-equivalence where pH = pKa, buffer regions, major species along the curve, and polyprotic steps.
candidates.include: Tag when a titration curve must be read, sketched or used, or the species present at a point in a titration identified.
candidates.exclude: Numerical species concentrations along polyprotic curves are not assessed.

candidates.name: Elementary reactions and molecularity
candidates.definition: Recognizing that an elementary step's rate law follows directly from its molecularity (unimolecular, bimolecular), unlike an overall reaction.
candidates.include: Tag when the rate law or molecularity of an elementary step must be written or identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag experimental rate laws for overall reactions (tag rate-law).

candidates.name: Endothermic and exothermic processes
candidates.definition: Identifying processes as endothermic or exothermic from temperature observations, the sign of q or ΔH, or energy diagrams, keeping system and surroundings distinct.
candidates.include: Tag when the direction of heat flow or the sign of ΔH must be determined from evidence or an energy diagram.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag energy profiles with activation barriers (tag activation-energy).

candidates.name: Ion-dipole attractions
candidates.definition: Attractions between ions and polar molecules, such as the orientation of water molecules around dissolved ions.
candidates.include: Tag when ion-dipole forces or hydration-shell orientation must be identified, drawn or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ionic bonding within a lattice (tag lattice-energy).

candidates.name: Chromatography and distillation
candidates.definition: Separating mixture components by differences in intermolecular attractions: paper or column chromatography (stationary versus mobile phase) and distillation by volatility.
candidates.include: Tag when a separation method is selected, explained or its results (such as a chromatogram) interpreted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag filtration of a precipitate as the only step of a gravimetric calculation.

candidates.name: Molecular polarity
candidates.definition: Deciding whether a molecule has a net dipole from its bond dipoles and three-dimensional shape.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must determine or justify whether a molecule is polar or nonpolar.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when polarity is stated in the question and only used to compare forces (tag the specific force).

candidates.name: Solubility and 'like dissolves like'
candidates.definition: Predicting and explaining solubility and miscibility from the relative strength of solute-solute, solvent-solvent and solute-solvent attractions.
candidates.include: Tag when solubility or miscibility must be predicted or explained from molecular structure and forces.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag Ksp calculations (tag solubility-product) or solubility rules for precipitates (tag precipitation).

candidates.name: Activation energy and energy profiles
candidates.definition: Reading single- and multi-step reaction energy profiles: activation energy, transition states, intermediates, forward and reverse barriers, the rate-limiting barrier, and overall ΔH.
candidates.include: Tag when an energy profile must be read, drawn or used, or activation energies compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple enthalpy diagrams with no activation barrier (tag endo-exothermic).

candidates.name: Molarity and solution preparation
candidates.definition: Calculating and using molar concentration (moles of solute per liter of solution), including preparing a solution of a target concentration.
candidates.include: Tag when molarity must be calculated, or moles found from molarity and volume as a substantive step.
candidates.exclude: Molality and percent-by-mass concentrations are not assessed (tag colligative-properties if present); dilution belongs to dilution.

candidates.name: Moles, molar mass and particle counts
candidates.definition: Converting among mass, moles and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number, including counting atoms within a formula.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must perform or reason about a mass-mole-particle conversion that is a substantive step, or the question is about the mole itself.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a mole conversion is an unremarkable first step of a larger stoichiometry, gas or solution calculation already captured by another concept, unless the question isolates it.

candidates.name: Rate laws and reaction order
candidates.definition: Determining reaction orders, the overall order, the rate constant and its units from experimental data, typically initial rates, and predicting rate changes when concentrations change.
candidates.include: Tag when orders, a rate law, k, or a predicted rate change must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag mechanism-based rate-law derivation (tag mechanism-rate-law) or integrated-rate-law graphs (tag integrated-rate-laws).

candidates.name: Acid-base reactions and mixtures
candidates.definition: Determining the products, major species and pH after mixing acids and bases, treating strong-reactant reactions as going to completion and handling the remaining excess or conjugate.
candidates.include: Tag when the composition or pH after mixing an acid and a base must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag titration-curve interpretation (tag titration-curves) unless a post-mixing calculation is required.

candidates.name: Buffers
candidates.definition: Identifying buffer components (a weak conjugate acid-base pair) and explaining how they consume added strong acid or base to resist pH change.
candidates.include: Tag when a buffer must be identified or prepared, or its response to added acid or base explained or written as an equation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag pH calculations of a buffer (tag henderson-hasselbalch) unless buffer behavior is also explained.

candidates.name: Calorimetry and specific heat
candidates.definition: Using q = mcΔT, heat capacity and calorimeter data to determine heat transferred or the enthalpy change of a process, and evaluating calorimetry procedures and errors.
candidates.include: Tag when calorimetry data or q = mcΔT must be used, or a calorimetry procedure or error analyzed.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag phase-change heat (q = nΔH) alone (tag phase-change-energy).
